title: Libby standard-of-care option row
description: One row per standard-of-care option assessed for the case by the standard_of_care_screener agent. An option qualifies only if it is FDA (or equivalent regulator) approved for a population that includes this patient, or is carried in a major academic / clinical-society guideline (NCCN, ESMO, ASCO, ASH, EHA, ASTRO, SITC and peers). This track is additive and runs parallel to the targetable-feature ranking: it never removes, reranks, or narrows the feature-targeted options the board and PI surface. Rows are researched, referenced, and rendered on the same footing as the biomarker-guided tracks.

soc_id.description: Stable kebab-case row id, conventionally <regimen shorthand>-<line> (e.g. 'carboplatin-etoposide-atezolizumab-1l', 'hypomethylating-venetoclax-1l').

option_label.description: The option as a treating oncologist would name it, including the full regimen where it is a combination (e.g. 'Azacitidine + venetoclax', 'Concurrent chemoradiation, cisplatin-based'). Rendered verbatim as the row heading.

option_aliases.description: Other names the same regimen travels under (protocol acronyms, trade names, guideline shorthand). Helps a reader match this row against their own notes.

category.description: Treatment modality. Standard of care is not only drugs: surgery, radiotherapy, locoregional therapy, transplant, and active surveillance are all legitimate standard options and are in scope for this track.

intent.description: The goal this option is pursued for in THIS patient's disease state. Do not carry over an intent from the option's original indication: the same regimen can be curative in one setting and palliative in another.

line_of_therapy.description: Where this option sits in the treatment sequence for this patient given prior_therapies[]. 'not_applicable' fits surgery, surveillance, and supportive care that are not indexed by line.

regulatory_status.description: Regulatory footing. 'not_fda_regulated' is the correct value for surgery, radiotherapy technique, and surveillance, which are standard of care by guideline rather than by approval. 'fda_approved_other_indication' alone does NOT make an option standard of care for this patient; it needs a guideline endorsement covering this population to qualify.

endorsements.description: What makes this standard of care. At least one entry is required: an option with no approval and no guideline carriage is not standard of care and belongs in the feature-targeted dossier or nowhere. List every independent endorsement found, rather than the single strongest one, so a reader can see whether the societies agree.

source.description: The body that carries the endorsement. Use 'other_society' for an indication-specific society not enumerated here and name it in `designation`.

designation.description: The endorsement as that body words it: 'Category 1', 'Category 2A', 'ESMO I, A', 'preferred regimen', 'on-label approval', 'recommended, moderate certainty'. Copy their vocabulary rather than translating it into a generic strength.

indication_text.description: The population the endorsement actually covers, in the source's own terms (histology, stage, line, biomarker, performance status). This is what a reader checks the patient against.

population_match.description: How the endorsed population lines up with THIS patient. The load-bearing honesty field: an approval or guideline entry written for a different stage, line, or biomarker subgroup is an extrapolation, and calling it a match is the failure mode that makes this whole report unsafe. 'partial_match' needs the discrepancy named in `rationale`.

version_or_date.description: Guideline version or approval date (e.g. 'NCCN v2.2026', 'FDA approval 2018-11'). Guidelines move; a claim without a version cannot be re-checked.

citation.description: Citation for this endorsement in the shared prefix form: 'guideline:*', 'fda:*', 'pmid:*', 'doi:*', 'nct:*', or a URL.

eligibility_status.description: Whether THIS patient can actually take this option, judged against profile.json only (prior_therapies[], stage, performance status, organ function, comorbidities, biomarkers). 'already_received' is the one that most often distinguishes a textbook option from a real one, and it is not inferable from the tumor type: read prior_therapies[]. 'unknown' is the correct answer when the profile is silent on the gating fact, and is never a synonym for eligible.

eligibility_rationale.description: 1-2 sentences citing the profile fields the eligibility call rests on. An 'unknown' row says which fact is missing.

blocking_factors.description: Specific facts that block or condition this option (prior exposure with progression, organ dysfunction, a comorbidity, an unmet biomarker gate). Required non-empty for conditionally_eligible, likely_ineligible, and contraindicated rows.

prior_exposure_note.description: Required (non-null) when eligibility_status is already_received: what the patient had, the best response, and why it stopped. Re-offering a regimen the patient already progressed on is the most damaging error this report can make, so the record has to be explicit rather than implied.

biomarker_requirement.description: Whether this option is gated on a biomarker result, and where that result stands in this case. Mirrors the biomarker-confirmation gating rule used by the targeted track.

threshold.description: The decision threshold the guideline or label names (e.g. 'PD-L1 CPS >= 1', 'HER2 IHC 3+ or ISH-amplified').

status_in_case.description: Required when `required` is true. 'not_measured' means nothing is on file, which is not the same as not_met; the distinction is the same one the biomarker survey turns on.

linked_survey_id.description: survey_id of the matching biomarker_survey.jsonl row when the gate is one the surveyor already logged, so the two reports point at each other instead of duplicating the gap.

evidence.description: The trials the endorsement rests on. One or two pivotal entries, not a literature dump: this report cites what makes the option standard, and the master manuscripts table carries the depth.

design.description: Study design in a phrase (e.g. 'randomized phase 3, open-label', 'single-arm phase 2').

effect_size.description: The result with its variance, as reported: 'median OS 14.7 vs 9.6 mo, HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.52-0.85)'. A point estimate with no interval is half a result; carry the interval when the paper gives one.

pmid.description: PubMed ID as a bare numeric string (no 'PMID:' prefix); null when the source has no PubMed record. Existence and contextual correctness are verified by the reference_checking skill, not this format gate.

doi.description: DOI in bare 10.xxxx/... form (no https:// or doi.org prefix); null when none.

toxicity_highlights.description: The toxicities that would actually change this patient's decision, weighted by preferences.json vetoes and by the comorbidities in profile.json. Not a label's full adverse-event table.

relationship_to_targeted_options.description: How this standard option sits alongside the feature-targeted options the board and PI ranked. This is the only sanctioned bridge between the two tracks, and it runs one way: it describes sequencing and conflicts, and never reranks or removes a targeted option.

relation.description: 'competes_for_same_line' and the two 'foreclose' values are the ones a treating team most needs to see: they mark a decision where taking one path costs the other (a regimen that would exhaust eligibility for a trial, or prior therapy that closes an enrollment window).

note.description: 1-2 sentences on the sequencing consequence. Names the interaction; does not advise which to choose.

related_intervention_ids.description: intervention_id values from recommendations.jsonl or the dossier that this option interacts with. Read-only pointers; this row never edits them.

consideration_status.description: The concrete next step for this option. 'requires_further_workup' is the correct value whenever a biomarker gate is unmet, unmeasured, or pending: an option behind an open gate is not yet actionable, and saying 'consider now' about it overstates what the record supports.

priority.description: How strongly a treating team should weigh this option for this patient now. essential: a guideline-preferred or on-label option for this exact population that the patient is eligible for and has not received. high: an endorsed alternative, or the preferred option behind one resolvable gate. medium: a later-line or partial-match option. low: carried for completeness (an option the patient is unlikely to be eligible for, or one whose endorsement covers a different population).

rationale.description: <= 3 sentences of clinician-facing prose: what the option is, what makes it standard for this patient, and the load-bearing caveat (a partial population match, an unmet gate, a prior exposure). Rendered verbatim into the report table, so write finished prose. No em-dashes (U+2014); the renderer's pre-flight blocks them.

references.description: pmid:* / doi:* / nct:* / guideline:* / fda:* citations supporting this row. Verified per .claude/snippets/reference_check.md before the row is written.

last_verified_utc.description: UTC date (YYYY-MM-DD) the endorsements on this row were last checked against the source. Required: guideline versions and approvals move, and a standard-of-care claim with no verification date cannot be trusted or re-checked.

supersedes.description: soc_id of a prior row this one corrects or replaces.
